Alyssa (CSM): Hey team, quick check-in on Kestrel onboarding. They're seeing occasional 95th pct latency spikes during morning batch jobs and a higher token cost than we projected. I ran a small perf profile this morning and have a few proactive recs: 1) try 4-bit quant on their small chat workload, 2) test swapping to the distilled-llama-7b variant for non-critical routes, and 3) add a regional low-latency routing policy for EU mornings. Want to coordinate a canary rollout this week.

Raj (ML Eng): Thanks Alyssa. Can you paste the profile output? rough numbers are enough. 95th and avg? Also what's their seq length distribution?

Alyssa (CSM): Sure — short summary: avg latency ~120ms, 95th ~340ms on hosted, peak token rate during batch ~6000 tokens/s, typical seq lengths 60-220 (median ~85). Cost per 1M tokens about $12 currently for the model they use.

Ben (SE): That 95th looks like tail latency from cold KV cache + occasional oversized batched requests. Two practical levers: quantize to q4_0 for the chat endpoint (gives ~1.6x throughput improvement in our perf harness) and split routes: keep current model for long-context routes, route short / interactive calls to distilled-llama-7b.

Raj (ML Eng): Agree. For quantization: we'll need to validate quality on their eval set. I can run a fast A/B on their top 200 prompts to check regression. If <2% drop in exact-match/acceptance we can proceed. I can also generate a small prompt-to-score mapping.

Alyssa (CSM): timeline? Kestrel is in onboarding ramp and renews in 10 months — want to reduce cost projection ASAP to lower renewal risk. We should do a canary next Tue.

Ben (SE): Canary plan outline: 1) spin up q4_0 variant pinned to model:v1-quant on Dedicated or Hosted low-traffic pool, 2) route 5% of interactive traffic via routing rule, 3) measure latency, token cost, and quality delta, 4) rollback if quality regression >2% or error rate jumps >0.5%.

Ben (SE): Example rollout config (for Redwood Console/CLI):
```json
{
  "route": "kestrel.chat.interactive",
  "policy": "canary",
  "weights": [ {"model": "distilled-llama-7b", "pct": 95}, {"model": "distilled-llama-7b-q4_0", "pct": 5} ],
  "metrics": ["latency_p95","token_cost","quality_score"]
}
```

optimize-bot: Automated suggestion: q4_0 quantization expected to reduce token compute by ~38% for this topology. Estimated cost delta: $12 -> $7.4 per 1M tokens. See /docs/quant-recs for details.

Raj (ML Eng): I'll run the eval against their 200 prompts today and post results. If quality delta <1.5% we'll recommend expanding to 20% traffic next week. Also propose a fallback policy to original model when avg latency >300ms for >2 minutes.

Alyssa (CSM): Perfect. I'll notify the Kestrel PM that we'll schedule a 30m enablement call Wed 10am to go over expected behavior and get their approval for canary. Also will capture customer feedback with a short form after the canary.

Ben (SE): One more ops note: ensure KV cache preload for their morning batch to avoid cold-start tail. We can add a quick cron job on their Dedicated pool to pre-warm top prefixes. Command example: `redwood cache prewarm --model model:v1-quant --prefix-file top-prefixes.txt --region eu-west-1`

Alyssa (CSM): Great. Next steps: Raj runs eval (today), Ben creates canary config and prewarm script (EOD), Alyssa schedules call + informs customer. Will update thread with results. :thumbsup:

Raj (ML Eng): Eval posted — quality delta 0.9% on acceptance metric, p95 improved ~28ms, no extra failures on top-200 suite.

Ben (SE): Canary config pushed to staging. Prewarm cron set. Scheduling canary for Tue 06:00 UTC.

Alyssa (CSM): Notified Kestrel PM; they approved Tue canary. I'll run the feedback form after 48h. If all good we'll scale to 20% then 50% over two weeks.

optimize-bot: Canary started at 1785429500. Monitoring metrics: latency_p95=310ms -> 270ms, token_cost delta ~-35%, quality_score delta -0.7%. No rollback triggers yet.

Alyssa (CSM): Awesome — marking as in-flight, will follow up after the 48h check-in.
